$comment: Entry schema for contributes.mcpServers (process plugins that declare the shell capability, manifest apiVersion 2). Host validation lives in backend/plugin/contrib_mcp_servers.go (install) and mcp_servers_launch.go (launch); the session rules live in backend/mcp/plugin_session.go. Each entry is a stdio Model Context Protocol server whose tools, resources and prompts the AI assistant can use. command is a bare program name found on the login PATH or ${pluginRoot}/<relative> (absolute paths are rejected); '${...}' in args and env values may only be {{lists.variables}}; there is no cwd: the server runs in the project root, or in the plugin root when requiresProject is false (such a server starts without a project and may not use ${projectRoot}). env values are literal (no ${env:VAR} expansion of host variables); env names on the contract denylist are rejected at install and at launch. A server starts only after the user confirms its exact command line (once per server spec; ${projectRoot} stays unexpanded in the fingerprint) in every approval mode, at most {{limits.restartsMax}} times per {{limits.restartWindowSeconds}} s per project (or without one) until the user restarts it; stderr is kept up to {{limits.stderrMaxBytes}} bytes. Calls to the server's tools follow the user's AI tool approval settings like any other MCP tool. Servers stop when the plugin is disabled, uninstalled, reloaded or upgraded, not when the plugin process stops. AI tools cannot start plugin MCP servers.
description: MCP servers: stdio Model Context Protocol servers for the AI assistant, started in the project root (or, with requiresProject false, without a project in the plugin root) after the user confirms the exact command line.

command.description: A bare program name such as "npx" or ${pluginRoot}/<relative path>. No shell runs in between: $VAR stays literal.

requiresProject.description: false for a server that does not work on a project (for example desktop automation): it runs in the plugin root, the AI assistant can use it in conversations without a project, and args/env may not use ${projectRoot}.
